# vishalakshi


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

vishalakshi keeps what you collect in one SQLite file on your own machine, called a vault, and lets you search it and ask questions of it. One question can draw on a paper, a web page, a talk transcript, your own notes and the source code on disk at once, and the answer cites the sections it used.

It is built from smaller packages. [fossick](https://github.com/vedicreader/fossick) fetches pages, papers and videos. [litesearch](https://github.com/Karthik777/litesearch) stores the text and finds it again by keyword and by meaning; a [`Vault`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/core.html#vault) is a litesearch [`Index`](https://Karthik777.github.io/litesearch/api.html#index), and its search defaults come from there. [Urai](https://github.com/vedicreader/urai) is the chat interface the vault talks to models through, and [Rishi](https://github.com/vedicreader/rishi) supplies the model backends. [kosha](https://github.com/vedicreader/kosha) indexes source code, and [rgapi](https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/rgapi) searches files on disk that nothing has indexed yet. [rahasya](https://vedicreader.github.io/rahasya/) finds personal information and [varga](https://vedicreader.github.io/varga/) recognises what kind of document something is.

## Install

``` sh
pip install vishalakshi
```

## Adding and searching

[`Vault()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/core.html#vault) with no argument opens `~/.vishalakshi/vault.db`. This page uses a throwaway file and fills it with this repository’s own docs and source.

``` python
from tempfile import mkdtemp
from litesearch import repo_root
from vishalakshi import Vault

root = str(repo_root() or Path('..'))   # works from nbs/ or the repo root
v = Vault(Path(mkdtemp())/'vault.db')
v.enc.note
```

    'minishlab/potion-multilingual-128M (256d, float16, model2vec)'

`add` takes a directory, a file or a piece of text. `grab` takes almost anything else, such as an arXiv id, a YouTube link, a GitHub repository, a PDF or a web address, and reads each the right way ([acquire](01_acquire.ipynb)). Adding a source that is already in the vault reads it again only when its content changed, and the result’s `changed` says whether it did. `note` writes your own note. A note with a `key=` or a title replaces the earlier note with the same key or title; a note with neither is added as a new one.

Every search result carries `age`, the seconds since its document was filed, and `stale`, which is True when the vault believes the document no longer matches its source. Stale results sort last. `poll()` (below) marks documents stale: a file that changed or vanished, a web page past its time limit that no watch refreshes, or an older copy that a watch has replaced. It deletes only documents that are both stale and replaced.

``` python
v.add(root)                       # README.md and every notebook under nbs/
v.note('federate fuses the legs by rank because they share no vector space: the vault embeds '
       'prose, kosha embeds identifiers, ripgrep embeds nothing.', tags=['retrieval', 'design'])
v.note('one document per key: writing it again replaces it', title='federation', key='federation')
v.stats()
```

To answer questions the vault needs a language model. The default is `gemma-4-E2B`, a small model that runs on this machine through LiteRT, on the GPU where there is one, and needs no API key. `model=` names any other model Rishi knows, local or hosted, and `chat_kw=` passes settings to it. `$VISHALAKSHI_MODEL` changes the default and `$VISHALAKSHI_GPU=0` keeps LiteRT on the CPU. `ask` retrieves the four best sections (`sections=4`), shows the model up to 1,500 characters of each (`max_chars=1500`), and returns the answer with [`cited`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/ask.html#cited), the sections the answer cites ([ask](02_ask.ipynb)).

``` python
r = v.ask('why are rankings fused instead of distances?')
print(r.model, '·', r.runtime)
print(r.answer)
print(L(r.cited).map(lambda c: f"{c['n']} {c['breadcrumb']}"))
if (hit := first(r.cited)): print(v.read(hit['node_id'])['text'][:400])
```

## Personal information and junk

A personal vault holds things that should not leave your machine: invoices, letters, bank statements. vishalakshi looks for personal information in everything it stores, with patterns and checksums rather than a model: email addresses, phone numbers, card and account numbers, national identity numbers, street addresses, dates of birth and API keys. On a held-out test set of 240 generated documents it missed nothing and raised no false alarm (`evals/RESULTS.md`). Names are harder. It finds only names that follow a title such as Dr or Mrs, and only when name detection is on (`ner=True`); a report’s `scanned_ner` says whether it looked.

What it finds sets each document’s privacy level: Open, Personal (an identifier was found, or someone marked it), or Local only (set by hand, or a sensitive type such as a passport or a payslip). Each shelf can also have a floor, a level none of its documents goes below. Before every model call the vault decides, with `send_check`, what each document may give a hosted model, meaning one that runs anywhere but this machine: an Open document goes whole, a Personal one masked or not at all, a Local only one never. A model on this machine may read everything. Each send to a hosted model is recorded in the vault’s send log. The details are on [pii](09_pii.ipynb).

Junk is a separate problem: cookie banners and site footers that match every search and answer nothing. `suggest_noisy` ranks likely junk without any labels (0.988 AUC on the test corpora) and `mark_noisy` takes a document out of search ([quality](10_quality.ipynb)).

``` python
from vishalakshi.pii import pii_report

r = pii_report('Invoice for ada@example.com. Card 4111 1111 1111 1111. KEY=sk-abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz123456')
r.has_pii, r.identifying, r.kinds
```

    (True,
     {'email': 1, 'card': 1, 'secret': 1},
     {'email': 1, 'card': 1, 'secret': 1})

``` python
# a person's judgement, over the top of the arithmetic
v.add('A letter about Jane, and what she said on Tuesday.',
      title='letter', source='/inbox/letter.md')
v.add('Cookie policy. All rights reserved. Privacy. Terms. Contact us.',
      title='footer', source='/inbox/footer.md')
v.mark_pii('/inbox/letter.md', reason='names a person')     # private even though nothing matched
v.mark_noisy('/inbox/footer.md', reason='site furniture')   # out of search, sections, context, ask

r = v.pii('/inbox/letter.md', ner=True)   # scanned_ner says whether names were looked for
r.scanned_ner, r.detected, r.has_pii, any('footer' in h['breadcrumb'] for h in v.search('cookie policy'))
```

| `pii=` in `ask` | what happens when the retrieved sections hold personal information |
|----|----|
| `local` | a model on this machine answers, told never to repeat a personal detail; if the model is not local, nothing is sent |
| `redact` | each recognised identifier is masked, then the named model answers, hosted or not. Names without a title, and the heading line above each section, are not masked |
| `refuse` | no model is asked, and the result says what was held back |

The default is `local` when a local runtime is installed and `redact` when not. `ask` cannot run with detection off: `pii='off'` warns and applies the default. The result’s `policy` says which was used, and any identifier the model repeats is masked in the answer. Under every policy a hosted model gets a Local only section only as a placeholder. Search and reading take `pii=` too (`off`, `redact` or `refuse`), and there the default is `off`, which returns the stored text.

``` python
v.mark_not_pii(doc_id, reason='my own invoice')          # a person clears a false alarm
v.set_level(doc_id, 'local')                              # never send this one to a hosted model
v.send_check(refs=[doc_id], model='gpt-4.1-nano').why     # what a send would do, in one sentence
v.accept_noisy(k=10, reason='reviewed')                   # mark the current top junk suggestions
v.fit_noise(save=True); v.use_noise(True)                 # optional: fit the junk score to your marks
```

## Paperwork

A document’s `kind` says how it arrived; its doctype says what it is, such as an invoice, a receipt, a contract, a paper or a payslip. `categorize` decides the doctype from cue phrases and figures in the text, and asks a model only when the cues cannot decide. `extract` pulls fields out of a document, such as an invoice’s number, vendor and total; without a `schema`, the doctype picks one. `ask_doc`, or `ask(ref=...)`, answers a question about named documents, read whole, with the rest of the vault behind them. More on [extract](06_extract.ipynb) and [ask](02_ask.ipynb).

``` python
INVOICE = '''# INVOICE
Invoice No: ACM-2024-0117
Date: 2024-03-01
Bill to: Contoso GmbH, Berlin
From: Acme Supplies Ltd
Total due: 1,240.00 EUR
Due date: 2024-03-31
Items: widgets x10 @ 124.00
'''
v.add(INVOICE, title='Acme invoice 0117', source='/inbox/acme-0117.md')
v.categorize_all(llm='never')
v.doctypes()
```

    {'code': 13, 'documentation': 4, 'invoice': 1, 'paper': 1, 'other': 1}

``` python
from dataclasses import fields
from vishalakshi.extract import SCHEMAS, as_schema

print(L(SCHEMAS), L(fields(as_schema('invoice'))).attrgot('name'))
e = v.extract('/inbox/acme-0117.md')                    # doctype picks schema
a = v.ask_doc('/inbox/acme-0117.md', 'what is owed, to whom, and by when?',
              schema='amount:float, payee:str, due:str')
e.schema, e.fields, a
```

## Code

`index_code` builds a [kosha](03_code.ipynb) index of a repository: its functions and classes, their names and the call graph. Once that index exists, `context` and `ask` add code sections beside the prose (`code=`). A code hit has no `node_id`; it is cited by `path:line` on disk. `grep` searches the files on disk with ripgrep and needs no index, and `federate` merges prose, code and ripgrep results into one ranking.

``` python
v.index_code(root)                # fills .kosha/; context then appends code sections
c = v.context('where do topic nodes get rebuilt?', sections=3, related=0, code=3, dir=root)
# code hits have no node_id; their handle is path:line on disk
c.code, L(c.results).filter(lambda r: r.node_id is None).attrgot('breadcrumb')
```

## Watches and the queue

A watch repeats an acquisition on a schedule. Its action is an acquisition method (`url`, `web`, `harvest`, `arxiv`, `youtube`, `crawl` or `path`), `remind` to write a note, or `folder`; `kind=` is the same thing under another name. A `folder` watch keeps a snapshot of a directory and fires with what was added, changed or removed, together with its `instructions` for whoever reviews the change. A schedule is `every='6h'` or `cron='0 9 * * 1'`, and [pobblebonk](https://vedicreader.github.io/pobblebonk/) keeps the schedules in the vault file.

`poll()` is the tick to call from cron or an app’s timer. It returns jobs whose worker died to the queue, queues the watches that are due, runs the queue, and every ten minutes runs `housekeep`. A failed fetch is retried with a growing delay and set aside as dead after five attempts; `jobs(state='dead')` lists those. See [jobs](11_jobs.ipynb).

``` python
v.watch('https://example.com/changelog', action='url', every='6h')
v.watch('late chunking retrieval', action='web', every='1d', n=5)
v.watch('Re-read the evals', action='remind', every='1w')
v.watch(Path(root)/'nbs', kind='folder', every='1h', instructions='flag any print() left in a notebook', pattern='*.ipynb')
L(v.watches()).map(lambda w: (w['kind'], w['target'][:34], w['every'], w['pattern']))
```

## Books and scans

A scanned book has no usable text layer, and an old print set in a legacy font may have one that reads as gibberish. [`read_doc`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/read.html#read_doc) reads a PDF or a page image page by page and picks a route for each page (`parse='auto'`): a text layer that passes its checks is kept, a scanned page is OCRed, and a page still scanned or flagged as garbled goes to a vision model, local or hosted. `preset=` picks the reading prompt (`generic`, `sanskrit`, `tamil` or `tables`), and `hint=` adds a sentence about the book. Given a folder, it reads every PDF and image under it. Each page’s text, route and flags are kept as numbered versions, so reading a page again with a better model (`reparse`) never loses the earlier reading. A page image cannot be masked, so a Personal page goes to a hosted model only with `allow=True`, and a Local only page never does. Readings are recorded and replayed through [`CachedChat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/ask.html#cachedchat), and a page with no recording yet reaches the model only when `$VISHALAKSHI_RECORD_CHAT` is set or a `chat=` is passed ([read](12_read.ipynb)).

`proofread` has other models read the pages again and files the word changes each reading would make. A change two readers agree on is `proposed`, and one that only one reader makes is in doubt. Nothing changes until the owner decides: `accept` applies changes as a new version of the page, `reject` sets them aside, and `undo_decision` and `revert_page` take decisions back ([proof](13_proof.ipynb)).

``` python
v.read_doc('books/', parse='auto', model='claude/sonnet', preset='sanskrit', hint='verses end in ॥ n ॥')
doc = v.read_doc('scan.pdf', parse='llm', model='gemini/gemini-2.5-flash')['doc_id']
v.pages(doc)                                   # text, route (text, ocr, model, proof), flags, version
v.reparse(doc, pages=[3, 4], model='claude/opus')
v.proofread(doc, ['claude/sonnet', 'gemini/gemini-2.5-pro'])
v.changes(doc, 'proposed'); v.accept(doc); print(v.proof_md(doc))
read_doc('scan.pdf', parse='auto', model='claude/sonnet')   # no vault: the pages alone
```

``` sh
vishalakshi grab https://example.com/post
vishalakshi ask "why does late chunking help"
```

| variable | what it sets |
|----|----|
| `$VISHALAKSHI_VAULT` | the vault file |
| `$VISHALAKSHI_MODEL` | the default model |
| `$VISHALAKSHI_PII_MODEL` | the local model that answers when sections are private |
| `$VISHALAKSHI_GPU=0` | keeps LiteRT on the CPU |
| `$VISHALAKSHI_OFFLINE` | never download a model; use the hashing encoder |
| `$VISHALAKSHI_CHAT_CACHE` | the folder [`CachedChat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/ask.html#cachedchat) records replies in |
| `$VISHALAKSHI_RECORD_CHAT` | lets [`CachedChat`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/ask.html#cachedchat) ask a real model when it has no recording |

The MCP client configuration is on [mcp](05_mcp.ipynb). Retrieval trade-offs and the measured defaults are in [concepts](07_concepts.ipynb) and [`evals/RESULTS.md`](../evals/RESULTS.md).

## Development

The notebooks in `nbs/` are the source, and `nbdev-export` writes the modules from them.

``` sh
pip install -e .
nbdev-prepare
```
